executiveSummary: Port operations risk remains elevated following a confirmed cyberattack on North Carolina Ports that forced manual processing across Wilmington, Morehead City, and the Charlotte inland port, demonstrating continued susceptibility of U.S. maritime logistics nodes to IT disruption View Article Supporting Report . Navigation and situational-awareness risk is sustained by ongoing GNSS interference. Industry research indicates hundreds of vessels are affected daily by jamming/spoofing, with impacts extending to GMDSS, radar, radios, NAVTEX, speed logs, clocks, and SATCOM-creating material safety and cyber-physical risk Source . A recent NAVCEN GUIDE entry confirms marine GPS interference in the Baltic Sea on 2026-08-14 Government Advisory . Government advisories continue to emphasize structural maritime cyber risks: MARAD warns about foreign-manufactured port equipment, remote service pathways, and logistics platforms (e.g., LOGINK, Nuctech, remotely serviceable ship-to-shore cranes), recommending segmentation, secure remote access, and reduced unnecessary communications Maritime Advisory . USCG clarifies MTSA cybersecurity requirements apply to inactive vessels with valid certificates, citing increased risks from unattended networks and vendor interfaces Government Advisory . Class guidance for ship cyber resilience (IACS UR E26/E27) is actively available from ClassNK, supporting operators in implementing governance and technical controls for onboard systems View Article . Outlook: Over the next 72 hours, analysts should monitor for residual port processing impacts and opportunistic targeting of logistics nodes; continued GNSS interference reports are likely; port facilities should reaffirm segmentation and remote-access controls per MARAD/USCG guidance. Confidence in this outlook is medium based on mixed incident and advisory reporting. Specific forecasts are not guaranteed. Facts reflect cited sources; risk judgments synthesize multiple records and standard maritime cyber operations knowledge.

descriptions: Navigation interference behaviors: GNSS jamming/spoofing resulting in loss of PNT integrity and dependent-system degradation (formal ATT&CK mapping not confirmed in sources).

Potential initial access vectors at ports/logistics: External remote services and third-party vendor access pathways (inferred from MARAD advisory and incident patterns; no specific technique IDs provided).
Operational impact behaviors: Loss of view/degraded situational awareness on the bridge; IT service disruption causing manual fallback in port operations.
